raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

When every response in a GRPO group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between the responses, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. Right now the float32 group statistics invent one instead: the group mean can land about an ulp away from the shared reward, the std is then about the same size as that residue, and the division amplifies it into the same nonzero advantage for every response in the group.

Measured on CPU against current main (group of 16 identical rewards of 0.3, reward on the last token):

- `compute_grpo_outcome_advantage`: advantage **+0.0289** for every response
- `compute_grpo_vectorized_outcome_advantage`: **+0.0289** here too, and worse at other group sizes (0.7 at group size 64 gives **-0.2937**, 0.9 gives **-0.3482**)

The Miles fork (RadixArk/miles) found and fixed the same class of problem on their side in RadixArk/miles#4019. This is the verl side of it: same idea, but both verl GRPO implementations, which share no code with the Miles one. I came across it while checking how uniform reward groups (all responses wrong in the same way, or a verifier that gives partial credit to all of them) flow through advantage computation.

Why this is not a duplicate of existing work:

- I searched open issues and PRs for this first (queries in the checklist below). Nothing open covers uniform groups getting nonzero advantages.
- #6348 (merged) fixed the neighbouring case: *near*-uniform, low-variance groups being scaled down in the vectorized path. Exactly uniform groups still slip through both implementations on current main, which the new tests show.
- #7964 (open) is about keeping RLOO vectorized advantages in the reward dtype, a different estimator and a different concern.

A note on assistance, per AGENTS.md: this change was drafted with AI help. I reviewed every line, the reproduction and the tests were run locally, and I am happy to defend or adjust any part of it.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Averl-project%2Fverl+uniform+rewards+advantage&type=issues and https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Averl-project%2Fverl+float32+advantage&type=issues
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

### Test

New tests in `tests/trainer/ppo/test_core_algos_on_cpu.py`:

- `test_grpo_uniform_reward_group_has_zero_advantage`: rewards 0.1, 0.3, 0.6, 0.7 and 0.9 at group sizes 8, 16 and 64, both implementations, with and without std normalization. All advantages and returns must be exactly zero. These fail on main with the values quoted above and pass with this change.
- `test_grpo_uniform_group_next_to_mixed_group`: a uniform group batched with a mixed [1, 0, 0, 0] group. Only the uniform group is zeroed; the mixed group keeps [1.5, -0.5, -0.5, -0.5].

Commands run locally (CPU):

```
pytest tests/trainer/ppo/test_core_algos_on_cpu.py -q
39 passed

pytest tests/trainer/ppo/test_core_algos_on_cpu.py -q -k grpo
20 passed, 19 deselected

ruff check verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py tests/trainer/ppo/test_core_algos_on_cpu.py
ruff format --check verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py tests/trainer/ppo/test_core_algos_on_cpu.py
both clean
```

### API and Usage Example

No API or config changes. Same call as before, now with the correct result for a uniform group:

```python
adv, _ = compute_grpo_outcome_advantage(token_level_rewards, response_mask, index)
# a group where every response scored 0.3 now gets advantages of exactly 0.0,
# instead of about +0.0289 for every response
```

### Design & Code Changes

`verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py` only, two places:

- `compute_grpo_outcome_advantage`: when a group's scores are all equal, use the shared score itself as the group mean (and std 1.0, like the singleton case). The centered scores are then exactly zero with or without std normalization, and no other group changes.
- `compute_grpo_vectorized_outcome_advantage`: after computing the scalars the same way as before, groups with more than one response whose min and max scores are equal are set to exactly zero, taken from the scores themselves rather than from the rounded statistics. Singleton groups keep the existing mean 0, std 1 convention.

`compute_gdpo_outcome_advantage` builds on the scalar GRPO function per reward dimension, so it picks up the fix for free. I kept this to GRPO on purpose: GPG divides by `f_norm` rather than a near-zero std, so the residue is not amplified there, and RLOO has its own open work (#7964). Happy to extend it if you would like them covered here too.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): ran `pre-commit run` on the two changed files; the checks that cover them (ruff, naming, compile) pass. A few repo-structure hooks need a full checkout and fail the same way on a clean tree, happy to rerun in CI.
- [ ] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs): no docs change needed, this only corrects computed advantages.
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code: the new tests live in `tests/trainer/ppo/test_core_algos_on_cpu.py`, which the CPU unit test workflow already runs.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in the `ci-request` channel in the verl Slack workspace: will do once this is out of draft.
- [ ] If your PR is related to the `recipe` submodule, please also update the reference to the submodule commit: not related.

Thank you for taking a look. This is my first PR here, so any guidance on shape or scope is very welcome.

files.patch:
@@ -280,6 +280,47 @@ def test_grpo_vectorized_matches_original_for_low_variance_rewards():
     assert torch.allclose(ret1, ret2, rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-6)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("reward", [0.1, 0.3, 0.6, 0.7, 0.9])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("group_size", [8, 16, 64])
+def test_grpo_uniform_reward_group_has_zero_advantage(reward: float, group_size: int):
+    # Every response in the group got the same fractional reward, so there
+    # is no preference between them and every advantage must be exactly
+    # zero. The float32 group statistics used to invent a small nonzero
+    # advantage for the whole group instead (up to ~0.35 for the
+    # vectorized path at group_size=64).
+    token_level_rewards = torch.full((group_size, 1), reward, dtype=torch.float32)
+    response_mask = torch.ones_like(token_level_rewards)
+    index = np.array(["prompt"] * group_size, dtype=object)
+
+    for fn in (compute_grpo_outcome_advantage, compute_grpo_vectorized_outcome_advantage):
+        for norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo in (True, False):
+            adv, ret = fn(
+                token_level_rewards=token_level_rewards,
+                response_mask=response_mask,
+                index=index,
+                norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo=norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo,
+            )
+            assert torch.equal(adv, torch.zeros_like(adv)), fn.__name__
+            assert torch.equal(ret, torch.zeros_like(ret)), fn.__name__
+
+
+def test_grpo_uniform_group_next_to_mixed_group():
+    # A uniform group in the same batch as a mixed group: only the
+    # uniform group's advantages are zeroed.
+    token_level_rewards = torch.tensor([[0.3], [0.3], [0.3], [0.3], [1.0], [0.0], [0.0], [0.0]], dtype=torch.float32)
+    response_mask = torch.ones_like(token_level_rewards)
+    index = np.array(["uniform"] * 4 + ["mixed"] * 4, dtype=object)
+
+    for fn in (compute_grpo_outcome_advantage, compute_grpo_vectorized_outcome_advantage):
+        adv, ret = fn(
+            token_level_rewards=token_level_rewards,
+            response_mask=response_mask,
+            index=index,
+        )
+        assert torch.equal(adv[:4], torch.zeros_like(adv[:4])), fn.__name__
+        assert torch.allclose(adv[4:, 0], torch.tensor([1.5, -0.5, -0.5, -0.5])), fn.__name__
+
+
 @pytest.mark.parametrize(
     "batch_size,seq_len,num_groups,seed",
     [

@@ -317,8 +317,18 @@ def compute_grpo_outcome_advantage(
                 id2std[idx] = torch.tensor(1.0)
             elif len(id2score[idx]) > 1:
                 scores_tensor = torch.stack(id2score[idx])
-                id2mean[idx] = torch.mean(scores_tensor)
-                id2std[idx] = torch.std(scores_tensor)
+                if (scores_tensor == scores_tensor[0]).all():
+                    # Every response in the group got the same reward, so
+                    # every advantage is exactly zero. Use the shared score
+                    # as the mean: the float32 mean of identical values can
+                    # land an ulp away from the value itself, and dividing
+                    # that residue by a near-zero std invents a small
+                    # nonzero advantage for the whole group.
+                    id2mean[idx] = scores_tensor[0]
+                    id2std[idx] = torch.tensor(1.0)
+                else:
+                    id2mean[idx] = torch.mean(scores_tensor)
+                    id2std[idx] = torch.std(scores_tensor)
             else:
                 raise ValueError(f"no score in prompt index: {idx}")
         for i in range(bsz):
@@ -349,11 +359,24 @@ def compute_grpo_vectorized_outcome_advantage(
     with torch.no_grad():
         scores = token_level_rewards.sum(dim=-1)
         g = as_torch_index(index, device=scores.device)
-        mean_g, std_g, _ = group_mean_std(scores, g, eps=0.0, device=scores.device)
+        mean_g, std_g, count_g = group_mean_std(scores, g, eps=0.0, device=scores.device)
         if norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo:
             scalars = (scores - mean_g[g]) / (std_g[g] + epsilon)
         else:
             scalars = scores - mean_g[g]
+        # A group whose scores are all the same carries no preference, so
+        # its advantages are exactly zero. The float32 group statistics
+        # above can leave a residue for such a group (a mean an ulp off, a
+        # std of the same size), which the division then amplifies, so
+        # zero those groups from the scores themselves.
+        num_groups = mean_g.shape[0]
+        group_max = torch.full((num_groups,), float("-inf"), device=scores.device, dtype=scores.dtype)
+        group_max.scatter_reduce_(0, g, scores, "amax", include_self=False)
+        group_min = torch.full((num_groups,), float("inf"), device=scores.device, dtype=scores.dtype)
+        group_min.scatter_reduce_(0, g, scores, "amin", include_self=False)
+        uniform = (group_max == group_min) & (count_g > 1)
+        if bool(uniform.any()):
+            scalars = torch.where(uniform[g], torch.zeros_like(scalars), scalars)
         advantages = scalars.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask
         return advantages, advantages

`378-379`: **🚀 Performance & Scalability** | **🔵 Trivial** | **💤 Low value** **Avoid the extra CUDA synchronization in the uniform-group mask.** For nonempty CUDA batches, `bool(uniform.any())` adds a host/device synchronization, including when no group is uniform. The preceding `group_mean_std` call already synchronizes, so this is a narrow optimization rather than removal of the only synchronization.
Suggested fix ```diff - if bool(uniform.any()): - scalars = torch.where(uniform[g], torch.zeros_like(scalars), scalars) + scalars.masked_fill_(uniform[g], 0) ```
The unconditional mask preserves the output. It also preserves autograd behavior because the function runs inside `torch.no_grad()`.
